observed_source_facts.fact: virtual/physical own their signal cleanup; outer main does not race their future. Only generic helper commands have outer Ctrl-C cancellation.
EventOutput/backend/bind occur before ctrl_c select at236; only SIGINT is handled, and stopped event after cleanup is outside that select.
Helper status/FD grants, from_sources, bind and EventOutput construction occur before ctrl_c select at100; no SIGTERM subscription.
stdout dedicated stdwriter thread owns bounded events only, channel2, per-event5s deadline; cancelled output remains in_flight and final output is skipped after shutdown.

shutdown sends stop and awaits listener. Listener drops listener, aborts+joins connection tree then awaits backend settle_closed with10s deadline. Dropping handle alone aborts tree and is not proof of awaited backend cleanup.
Physical begin_close drains event buffers then marks network_closed and requests close. Worker independently cancels/reaps/checked-releases and restores before zeroing permits/state.
restore awaited before state available/cleanup_verified. Response budget is retained until network close. Quarantined/error paths are not reusable restoration success.
Virtual close clears pending/events and drops owned lease; DeviceLease Drop resets configuration/queues/pending and leased=false.
Existing local subprocess test uses one imported virtual lease,4096pipe+100snapshots,0.2s sleep then SIGINT/deadline; it does not handle TERM or assert a real pending URB/both profiles.

minimal_signal_contract: Create Unix SIGINT+SIGTERM subscriptions synchronously before the first await or device/helper/listener acquisition; merely constructing a lazy ctrl_c future does not prove early registration.

Keep subscriptions owned through setup, operations, shutdown and final event. A received signal must request cooperative cleanup and await server.shutdown; do not let outer main or second signal drop/abort cleanup future.

Signal during failed/blocked ready output must still reach listener/lease cleanup. Final stopped output after successful cleanup may be skipped or cancelled under known backpressure rather than reblocking the same writer.

Successful normal output must expose stopped only after backend cleanup; failure/quarantine reports nonzero and must not claim available/original restoration. SIGKILL/process crash recovery remains explicitly excluded.

backpressure_determinism: Verify real pipe capacity with F_GETPIPE_SZ and unread occupancy; no0.2s-only assumption of a blocked writer. Small atomic event writes can block before occupancy reaches4096, so100snapshot count alone does not prove exactly-full capacity.

If an exact4096full state is required, use a test-owned pipe, retain its blocking writer in parent, drain ready/pre-snapshot, then fill the known-empty pipe with4096test filler before enqueueing one snapshot; verify FIONREAD==capacity and never drain afterward. Do not set O_NONBLOCK on shared writer OFD inherited by child, which would turn the child write into EAGAIN instead of blocking.

A physically full pipe establishes consumer backpressure, not an exact Rust await instruction. If claiming writer-inflight, require a Linux-only observable blocked writer witness or explicit private test receipt; otherwise word coverage accurately.

Do not invent a stopped event that was intentionally skipped.
